summary: Full backend + frontend regression of OpusPawClaw Mission Control. 11/11 pytest tests pass (incl. real Emergent-bridged Hermes chat completion). Playwright e2e covered AgeGate -> Mission -> Chat -> all sidebar modes, verified 7 pills, 6 agents, 4 DAO tokens, 10 buckets, Paperclip, GitPanel, and real bridged LLM responses with X-Hermes-Provider / X-Hermes-Real-Model / X-Hermes-Latency-Ms surfaced to UI. Doctrine sweep (no 'Haiku' / 'donate' / 'donation' / 'solicitation') clean across every tested endpoint and across the rendered UI.

minor.issue: Runs bridge call via asyncio.run() inside asyncio.to_thread — works today but is fragile if emergentintegrations ever spawns long-lived loop state; acceptable for mirror scope.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 353 lines — still within the 700-line limit but approaching the point where Hermes bridge, Paperclip mirror, DAO/system fixtures, and git helpers should each move into their own module for maintainability.

_bridge_via_emergent uses asyncio.run() inside an asyncio.to_thread worker. Safe because the worker has no event loop, but a direct `await chat.send_message(...)` in the outer async handler (dropping to_thread) would be simpler and avoids a nested-loop class of bugs.
Hermes refresh polling is correctly paused on document.hidden and uses a 4s AbortController as required. Chat-completions widened to 60s to accommodate real bridge latency — good.
All interactive elements have data-testid attributes; accessibility is solid.
No hardcoded URLs — frontend uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL; backend uses MONGO_URL/DB_NAME/EMERGENT_LLM_KEY exclusively.
Doctrine rules (no Haiku/donate/donation/solicitation, only 'Opus' Anthropic label, palette restricted, #UntilNoKidInNeed visible) are all honored in source and runtime responses.
test_credentials: N/A — app has no auth layer; AgeGate is a client-side acknowledgement only.
seed_data_creation: None; all endpoints return static mirror data. Mongo status_checks untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_mission_control.py and already validate the doctrine sweep globally. If you need to re-run quickly: `cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_mission_control.py -v`. The 'fast' virtual model bridges to gemini-2.5-flash (~600ms-1s) and is the cheapest way to verify the Emergent bridge still works. X-Hermes-Provider / X-Hermes-Real-Model / X-Hermes-Latency-Ms are exposed through CORS expose_headers so fetch() from the browser can read them.
rca of the issue: No defects found. One initial self-inflicted test-logic bug in the git-status assertion (substring match 'ackend/server.py' accidentally matched the valid 'backend/server.py') was fixed inside the test file itself (now uses startswith), and the test now passes against real API output.
